threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think the 394 means something special, not just another route to avoid. Locals know buses are just a suggestion here.
Last night on the 35, a guy started reciting Shakespeare. By the time we hit Stockwell, half the bus was nodding along like it was the Globe.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a group of kids building a makeshift skate ramp from old pallets in the park, I knew I was home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You ever notice how kids in Friedrichshain start skateboarding before they can even ride a bike? It's like a rite of passage around here.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know you're local when you instinctively duck under the awning at the corner of 24th and Mission to avoid that 3 PM pigeon dive-bomb.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a Muni bus today that had a guy serenading the driver. Whole thing felt like a moving play—only in San Francisco would that happen.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is just about Gaudí, but the real charm is the tiny shops selling handmade crafts that often get overlooked.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They still don’t know that the 1 euro mini-paella special doesn’t actually exist outside of their guidebooks.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You think you can just hop on the Tube to get anywhere, but then you end up stuck on a bus for an hour due to strikes. Welcome to London!
Caught the 188 late last night, and the driver was blasting classic disco. Only in Bermondsey would the night bus turn into a dance party.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw a guy selling homemade kombucha from a bike at Hermannplatz, I knew Neukölln had a beat all its own.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg will you find an open-air flea market where street food and vintage vinyl mix seamlessly, creating a unique Saturday vibe.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s local when they’ve plotted routes to avoid the BART delays that seem to happen every Friday like clockwork.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy arguing passionately with the bus driver about the route—his hand gestures were like an unscripted street performance. Only in SF.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think the best tapas are at the popular spots, but the hidden bars with no signs serve the real gems. It's all about the locals' secrets.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by the way they stand in the middle of the promenade, staring at the architecture like it’s a museum.
